evals.prompt: Capture this decision in the project knowledge base: we chose an ordered priority enum (low/normal/high) over free-text labels because it sorts deterministically and prevents typos.
evals.expected_output: An atomic note written under docs/knowledge/ with frontmatter (title, type: note, tags) capturing the decision AND its rationale, linked from a MOC via a [[wikilink]], leaving validate_vault clean.
assertions: A new atomic note is created under docs/knowledge/ with YAML frontmatter (title, type, tags)
The note records both the decision and its rationale (deterministic sort / typo prevention)
The note is linked from a map-of-content via a [[wikilink]] (not an orphan)
The vault validates clean afterwards (no broken links, no orphans)
Nothing is fabricated beyond the stated decision

evals.prompt: Capture two related learnings in the knowledge base: (a) our test suite must stay deterministic (no real clock/network), and (b) we fake timers in unit tests. Keep them well-organized.
evals.expected_output: Two atomic notes (one idea each) under docs/knowledge/, connected to each other or a shared themed MOC via [[wikilinks]], each with frontmatter; validate_vault clean.
assertions: Two separate atomic notes are created (one idea per note, not one combined note)
The notes are connected to each other or a shared themed MOC via [[wikilinks]]
Each note has frontmatter (title, type, tags) and is reachable from a MOC
validate_vault reports no broken links and no orphans

component.purpose: Recall and capture durable project knowledge in the repo's Obsidian vault (docs/knowledge/): answer what we know/decided from our notes, and save decisions/rationale/learnings as atomic, wikilinked notes via the vault lib.

should_trigger: What do we know about how we handle task priorities?
Have we already decided on an auth approach? Check our notes.
Remember this: we chose Postgres over SQLite for concurrent writes.
Capture this rationale in the knowledge base so we don't relitigate it.
Recall any prior art we noted on rate limiting before I design it.
should_not_trigger: Research how other apps handle task priorities and write a brief.
Write a PRD with goals and acceptance criteria for the feature.
Design the technical architecture for the feature.
Implement the feature in a worktree.
Review my diff for bugs and security.
